claims.text: As-cast or homogenized NiFeCoCr-based high-entropy alloys have a largely random chemical distribution.
Adding approximately 5 at.% Pd and applying optimized heat treatment enhances short-range chemical order in NiFeCoCr-based high-entropy alloys.
Pd facilitates chemical ordering during annealing.
Enhanced short-range chemical order makes the distribution of magnetic exchange energies more uniform.
A narrower distribution of magnetic exchange interactions produces a smooth, second-order magnetic phase transition.
The Pd-and-annealing modification reduces domain-wall pinning.
Reduced domain-wall pinning enables a strong magnetocaloric response at applied fields below 1 T.
Reduced domain-wall pinning lowers magnetic hysteresis.
The proposed magnetic-ordering mechanism supports rapid heat exchange.
The proposed modification preserves mechanical stability.
Optimally heat-treated, Pd-doped material will have a sharper magnetocaloric peak than the baseline.
Optimally heat-treated, Pd-doped material will have approximately 40% greater refrigerant capacity than the baseline.
Optimally heat-treated, Pd-doped material will exhibit less magnetic hysteresis than the baseline.
Optimally heat-treated, Pd-doped material will maintain or improve mechanical stability relative to the baseline.
The hypothesis is expected to hold from 150 to 400 K at applied magnetic fields below 1 T.
Excessive grain growth, phase segregation, or inhomogeneous Pd distribution could prevent homogenization of magnetic exchange interactions.
